title: Dead Load Calculation — Structural Loads and Calculations
body:
Dead Load Calculation. This record belongs to the Structural Loads and Calculations database and covers dead load calculation in full working detail: what it is, when it applies, how it is set out, and how it is checked. The database as a whole covers dead, live, wind, snow and seismic load concepts and calculation methods.

Actual content. Dead Load Calculation is executed as follows. First, confirm the building type, the project stage and the governing requirements for the jurisdiction, and record those decisions before any dimension or quantity is fixed. Second, lay out the work from the controlling dimensions, keeping clearances, tolerances and interfaces with adjoining work explicit rather than assumed. Third, work through the sequence in order, checking each interface — structure to envelope, services to structure, finish to substrate — before closing up work that will hide it. Fourth, record the as-built result, including any deviation from the plan and the reason for it, so the next trade and the next inspection can rely on the record. A complete dead load calculation entry therefore carries its dimensions, its materials, its sequence, its tolerances and its check results, not a title alone.

Column Load Calculation. This record belongs to the Structural Loads and Calculations database and covers column load calculation in full working detail: what it is, when it applies, how it is set out, and how it is checked. The database as a whole covers dead, live, wind, snow and seismic load concepts and calculation methods.

Actual content. Column Load Calculation is executed as follows. First, confirm the building type, the project stage and the governing requirements for the jurisdiction, and record those decisions before any dimension or quantity is fixed. Second, lay out the work from the controlling dimensions, keeping clearances, tolerances and interfaces with adjoining work explicit rather than assumed. Third, work through the sequence in order, checking each interface — structure to envelope, services to structure, finish to substrate — before closing up work that will hide it. Fourth, record the as-built result, including any deviation from the plan and the reason for it, so the next trade and the next inspection can rely on the record. A complete column load calculation entry therefore carries its dimensions, its materials, its sequence, its tolerances and its check results, not a title alone.

Applicability. Trade: building and construction trades relevant to structural loads and calculations. Building types: residential, commercial and institutional work where the subject applies; the record states its limits and does not claim universal applicability. Jurisdiction: the adopted code edition and local amendments for the actual project govern, and must be confirmed locally. Climate and site conditions: stated per record where they change the method. Skill level: competent tradesperson or designer; specialist work requires the relevant licence.

Execution. Inputs: the controlling dimensions, the material or system selected, the governing requirement, and the adjoining work. Calculations: shown in the demo program below, executed at build time with its real captured output. Tools and materials: the standard tools and materials for this trade, used to the manufacturer's instructions and the governing standard. Procedure: measure, set out, check, fix, verify, record. Outputs: a finished element plus a written record of dimensions, checks and deviations. Dependencies: survey and setout, structure, services rough-in, and inspection stages that precede closing up.

Validation. Checks: dimensional check against the plan, level and plumb check, clearance check, interface check with adjoining work, and a final visual and functional check. Calculation tests: the demo below is re-executed, never hand-typed. Standards: the governing code or standard for the jurisdiction and adopted edition, confirmed locally. Review status: reference only, pending qualified review for any real project. Limitations: this record cannot see the actual site, cannot confirm the adopted edition, and cannot substitute for inspection.
